title: 2026 UK ETS CCS boundary-metering consultation QA controls

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme: Regulating cross-boundary CCS pipelines
UK ETS: Regulating cross-boundary CCS pipelines (accessible webpage)

facts.source_fact: If OPRED became sole offshore regulator under the consulted Option 2, monitoring infrastructure would be required at the regulatory transfer boundary.
The consultation names CEMS or AMS as examples of monitoring infrastructure.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve instrument examples without mandating one.

facts.source_fact: Operators must annually report CO2 lost through venting, leakage and fugitive emissions under the current accounting context described.
Operators also report the quantity of CO2 transported to offshore storage.
The regulator boundary provides end and start points for accounting between regulators.
Existing onshore monitoring could potentially serve as the designated last onshore meter.
Alternatively additional metering could be installed near the pipeline beachhead.
The consultation recommends a proposed transfer location no more than 2 km from mean high-water springs for the described option.
facts.expected_handling: Do not present 2 km as commenced legal limit.

facts.source_fact: Consultation questions explicitly seek stakeholder views on dedicated metering and transfer-point distance.
The Authority states the options are intended to reduce monitoring infrastructure and administrative burden, but cost savings were not quantified.
